# Third-party notices

The `kestrel-native` wheel links the following Rust audio dependency closure.
Versions are pinned by `Cargo.lock`; repository links provide the corresponding
source code. The full MPL-2.0, MIT, and Apache-2.0 license texts and the exact
libopus notice are shipped in the adjacent `licenses/` directory.

## Rubato 4.0.0 and FFT/audio adapter closure

The following dependencies are used under their MIT option:

- `rubato 4.0.0`, `audioadapter 4.0.0`, `audioadapter-buffers 4.0.0`, and
  `audioadapter-sample 4.0.0` — Copyright (c) 2020 or 2026 Henrik Enquist;
- `realfft 3.5.0` — Copyright (c) 2020 Henrik Enquist;
- `windowfunctions 0.1.1` — Copyright (c) 2025 Henrik Enquist;
- `rustfft 6.4.1` and `strength_reduce 0.2.4` — Copyright (c) 2015 The
  RustFFT Developers;
- `transpose 0.2.3` — Copyright (c) 2022 The transpose Developers;
- `primal-check 0.3.4` — Copyright (c) 2014 Huon Wilson;
- `lazy_static 1.5.0` and `regex-lite 0.1.9` — Copyright (c) The Rust
  Project Developers;
- `visibility 0.1.1` — Copyright (c) 2024 Daniel Henry-Mantilla;
- `extended 0.1.0` — Copyright 2022 Dietrich Epp.

`audio-core 0.2.1` is also available under `MIT OR Apache-2.0`; this
distribution uses the Apache-2.0 option because its crate archive does not
ship a separate MIT notice. The remaining transitive numerical dependencies
were already present in `kestrel-native` before the audio feature and retain
their upstream license terms.

## Opus decoder

`symphonia-adapter-libopus 0.3.0` is used under its MIT option. It links
`opusic-sys 0.7.5`, whose default bundled build compiles the unmodified libopus
source included in that immutable crate archive. The adapter adds no license
family beyond the MIT text already shipped in `licenses/`. Libopus is used
under its BSD-style license and royalty-free patent grants; its exact notice
is shipped as `licenses/OPUS.txt`. No system Opus library is required at
runtime.

## Platform file-admission dependencies

`libc 0.2.186`, `windows-sys 0.61.2`, and its `windows-link 0.2.1`
dependency are used under their `MIT OR Apache-2.0` terms for nonblocking,
handle-based regular-file admission. These dependencies add no license family
beyond the MIT and Apache-2.0 texts already shipped in `licenses/`.
